source.display_title: 05/16/2026 - Kurt Wollenhaupt x Harry Edmonds  — Follow Up

rep.name: Harry Edmonds
rep.location: London, UK (self-described nomadic, moving country roughly every three months)

prospect.name: Kurt Wollenhaupt
prospect.location: Hawaii, USA (staying at his mother's farm at the time of the call, returning home on the 15th of the following month)
prospect.occupation: Owns a two-acre flower farm in Hawaii
prospect.family_status: Mother living; staying at her house. No partner or children mentioned.
prospect.training_background: Trained kettlebells in gym classes until they stopped after COVID and never restarted; was 'doing great back in last October'. Gym member at home. Could do pull-ups before the illness. Has not trained since November — tried a few times and lasted five minutes. Currently on body-weight exercise only, cleared to begin light loads.
prospect.medical: Contracted traveller's diarrhoea hiking in Bhutan/Thailand; antibiotics wiped out gut flora and Clostridioides difficile took over. A second course of antibiotics failed, requiring a faecal matter transplant, which appears to have worked. In active rehabilitation with three doctors, with three to six months of recovery remaining before the gut is 'locked in'. Prescribed a staged loading protocol using stool consistency as the tolerance marker. Reports central adiposity gained during the illness.

signals: In the middle of a serious active health event rather than recovering from a bad season — three to six months of gut rehabilitation still ahead, post-faecal-transplant
Explicitly frames training as part of the treatment: 'the healing process is much better for the people who do weight-bearing exercise'
Names the clinical stake himself: 'sarcopenia is a big problem with people who start aging, muscle-wasting, if they don't push it'

Alternative read is the_preserver — 65, exceptionally health-literate, already medically managed by three physicians, land-owning, no price resistance shown. The deciding factor for prehab_fighter is that the health event is active and ongoing, not past.

goals.text: Rebuild strength back to roughly where he was before the illness
Get rid of the abdominal fat that settled during the illness
Prevent sarcopenia and age-related muscle wasting by progressively loading again
Learn correct technique on the technical lifts, especially snatches and swings, having seen people do them badly in class
Be able to train at home on his own land rather than at a gym full of people on their phones

pains.text: Post-C.-difficile recovery following a faecal matter transplant, with three to six months still to run before the gut stabilises
Has not trained since November; attempts ended after five minutes because he was worn out
Weight did not drop as expected during the illness and has redistributed to the stomach
Kettlebell classes at his gym stopped after COVID and never restarted, removing his structure and his coaching
Currently at his mother's farm with no gym access for another month
Concerned about form on technical lifts: 'we've had kettlebell classes and people are going and all over... Especially when there's things like snatches'

objections.raw_quote: So yeah, I'm not sure that this program right now, but I just wanted to kind of see if, you know, after a great program.
objections.rep_response: Agreed with the objection rather than working it, and reinforced it: 'I also don't want you to pay for something that you can't use right now.' Proposed reconnecting a week after the prospect returns home and tests himself in the gym.

objections.raw_quote: but it will be more useful once i get finished with this healing and then once i get back to the gym for a couple weeks so that you know okay i'm back to pretty much where i was
objections.rep_response: Accepted it. Repeated the plan to reconnect in about five weeks and stay in touch in the meantime.

evidence: The rep, not the prospect, closed the door on buying today: 'let's schedule something in for a week after you get back. You go to the gym and see if you're all good. If you're all good, let's talk about it... But I also don't want you to pay for something that you can't use right now.'
Concrete re-engagement plan agreed: 'we can catch up in five weeks or so' / 'Okay. Sounds great.'
Buying signals present and unaddressed: 'So you take credit card, I presume you just take a credit card' and 'Well, I think you can help me, I don't know, I think.'
Counter-evidence: no date was actually booked, no calendar invite, no payment link. The follow-up rests on the rep remembering to reach out ('I'm going to make a note of you on my [CRM]').
outcome.next_step: Prospect returns home on the 15th of the following month, tests himself in his gym for about a week, then reconnects with the rep in roughly five weeks. Rep to stay in touch in the interim. No date booked.

notable.note: The rep voluntarily declined to take money from a willing, solvent prospect on clinical-timing grounds — 'I also don't want you to pay for something that you can't use right now' — after the prospect had effectively pre-offered his credit card. That is the correct call and the opposite of the pattern this audit is looking for; it should be recorded as a positive exemplar. Two offsetting problems: the rep still gave specific kettlebell purchase weights (2x15 lb and 2x24 lb) for immediate home use during active post-transplant recovery, and asserted '100%. 100%.' that the training would remove the prospect's abdominal fat. Separately, roughly a third of the call — from about 00:17 to 00:28 — was the rep's own travel plans, house purchase in Japan, tattoos and girlfriend, during which no discovery was done at all.

quality.notes: Persistent inversion. Blocks labelled Kurt contain clear rep lines ('Well, I think we can, but I want to make'; 'Whereabouts are you in the States?') and blocks labelled Harry contain clear prospect lines ('I'm 65'; 'I go back on the 15th of next month'; 'Hawaii'). The 00:15:58 block runs both sides together including the entire price quote. Roles were read from content throughout.
